clips.title: The story
paras: Coleman Farthing of Brill seeks vengeance against his former landowners, the Agamands, by having their restless undead remains collected and destroyed. This task sends you north to Agamand Mills to put down Devlin Agamand, the sharp-tongued younger son of the estate. It begins a bitter vendetta against the family who failed to protect Tirisfal's common folk from the Plague.

Before the Third War, Agamand Mills stood as the breadbasket of northern Tirisfal, owned by a wealthy landed family. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, the common folk looked to the noble landowners for safety, only to find neither sanctuary nor salvation. Coleman Farthing survived in undeath, but his heart remains consumed by hatred for the family he served. Rather than letting them roam in eternal torment, Farthing desires the morbid satisfaction of collecting their bones to desecrate them under his own heel.

Devlin Agamand was the younger brother of Thurman Agamand. In life, Devlin was widely remembered as a weak, spiteful, and sharp-tongued youth who stood in stark contrast to his gentle elder brother. When the Plague of Undeath crept into the mill estate, Devlin was among the quickest to fall prey to the corruption. Now, stripped of whatever fragile wit he possessed in life, his mindless corpse chatters incessantly along the northern road leading into the family mills.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Devlin Agamand was the younger of two sons in the Agamand family, and in life the two could not be more different. Thurman was tall and gentle while his younger brother was weak and sharp tongued.
When Agamand Mills fell to the Plague, I was not surprised to hear that Devlin was quick to succumb. His mad chattering can still be heard near the road leading to the Agamand Mills.
I'm collecting the remains of the Agamands, and I want poor Devlin. Find him, destroy him, and bring me his bones.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Thank you. Devlin's bones will rest nicely on my mantle.
If my cold heart can find warmth, it is in knowing that the Agamands are destroyed. They failed me and my family when the Plague came - now I swear I will smash their remains under my heel!
